thread:
incidents-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty: SEV2 - GPU queue growth alert for prod-eu-west (queue depth > 800, +320% over baseline). Auto-created channel and paged oncall. See runbook: https://internal/runbooks/gpu-queue-exhaustion
ryan-oncall: Acknowledged. I'm looking at the dashboard now. CPU/GPU utilization shows pools hitting 'max_replicas' caps, autoscaler shows repeated backoff loops.
anjali: I can pull autoscaler logs and cloud API responses. I think I saw some 4xx errors earlier.
mike: Observed large spike from a tenant replay job around 17:12 UTC, likely the initial surge.
ryan-oncall: Copy. Starting triage — key goals: (1) stop customer impact, (2) add capacity, (3) identify root cause for autoscaler not increasing.
ryan-oncall: Metrics: queue depth time-series attached (snippet):```queue_depth ~ 820 @ 17:18, 940 @ 17:23, 1150 @ 17:27```
anjali: Autoscaler-controller logs show repeated requests to cloud provider returning 403/QuotaExceeded for GPU cores in eu-west-1a. Example log:```E 17:19 autoscaler_controller.go: request failed: CreateInstance: 403 QuotaExceeded: "Requested 8 GPUs, available 0 in zone eu-west-1a"```
kate: So autoscaler is healthy but hitting quota on a single AZ. Do we have cross-AZ capacity?
ryan-oncall: Good question. Routing currently pins jobs to pools in eu-west-1a (affinity), so requests can't easily fall back to eu-west-1b until routing policy updates. That explains local saturation.
remy-product: Customer impact note — a handful of enterprise tenants reported 429s and elevated latency. CS: prioritize comms for any paying tenants > p75 latency increase.
cs-elaine: I'm compiling affected tenants. So far 6 tenants with sustained errors since ~17:20. I'll draft a status update if we have mitigation plan.
mike: Immediate mitigation options: (A) ask cloud to raise GPU quota in eu-west-1a (slow), (B) change routing to allow eu-west-1b pool to accept traffic (fast), (C) manually scale dedicated standby pool in eu-west-1b and re-route.
ryan-oncall: I'll do (B)+(C) now: enable cross-AZ fallback and spin up manual replicas in eu-west-1b standby pool. Doing manual scale:```kubectl -n prod-eu scale deployment inference-gpu-eu-west-1b --replicas=6```
ryan-oncall: K8s command applied, starting node provisioning. Logs are showing instances provisioning in eu-west-1b.
anjali: Confirming autoscaler attempted to create instances in 1a, got quota errors. When I toggle routing to prefer any healthy eu-west AZ, traffic begins moving to existing running capacity in 1b.
ryan-oncall: I've updated routing policy in the router service:```PATCH /v1/routing/pools/prod-eu -d '{"preferred_zones": [], "failover": true}'``` -> router accepted change.
ryan-oncall: Queue depth is dropping: 1150 -> 600 -> 220 over next 6 minutes. Latency p95 down from 2.8s to 0.9s.
cs-elaine: Notifying affected tenants with interim message: "We're mitigating a GPU capacity issue in eu-west; traffic is being routed to alternate capacity and we expect service to normalize shortly." Sending now.
remy-product: Good. Any risk of oscillation once standby capacity drains? We should throttle heavy replays to avoid re-saturating.
kate: We have queue admission controls — recommend enabling soft-shed (priority-based) on the offending tenant(s) until quota is lifted.
ryan-oncall: Enabling soft-shed for tenant IDs: T-331, T-442. Command:```curl -XPOST https://internal-api/queues/tenants/T-331/shed -d '{"mode":"soft","threshold":0.7}' -H 'Authorization: Bearer REDACTED'```
anjali: Confirmed soft-shed in effect for those tenants. Their request rates dropped ~60%. Queue stabilized.
infra-jen: FYI I've opened a support case with cloud provider to request quota increase for eu-west-1a and asked for expedited review. Case ID: CL-102334. ETA unknown.
mike: Good. For longer-term: routing affinity to single AZ is risky. We should add runbook step to ensure new pools never rely on single-AZ pinning.
ryan-oncall: Agreed. Current incident mitigation summary: manual scale in eu-west-1b, router fallback enabled, soft-shed applied to top noisy tenants, cloud quota case opened. Customer-facing update sent.
remy-product: Requesting a short post-incident note for affected enterprise customers with root cause and remediation timeline. Who owns?
cs-elaine: I'll own the email once we have root cause + timeline from infra and eng.
anjali: Root cause initial hypothesis: deployments had AZ affinity set during a recent rollout to reduce inter-AZ traffic costs; combined with an unexpected tenant replay, that created a hot-spot. Autoscaler behaved correctly but was blocked by per-AZ GPU quota.
kate: Action items (initial):
- A1: Remove strict AZ affinity from inference pools and enable multi-AZ failover by default (owner: kate, due: 72h).
- A2: Add autoscaler metric alert for repeated cloud API 4xx/QuotaExceeded errors and escalate sooner (owner: anjali, due: 48h).
- A3: Create runbook entry to manually flip router failover and to scale standby pools during surge (owner: ryan-oncall -> eng-sre, due: 24h).
- A4: CS customer comms + postmortem draft (owner: cs-elaine, due: 24h).
- A5: Request provider quota increase and track CL-102334 (owner: infra-jen, due: monitor until closed).
- A6: Add admission control rate limits for very large tenant jobs / replays (owner: mike, due: 7 days).
ryan-oncall: I'll open a postmortem ticket and schedule the blameless postmortem meeting for tomorrow 09:30 UTC. Ticket: PM-7882.
remy-product: Please include traffic samples and tenant replay pattern in the postmortem.
cs-elaine: Draft of external note ready to review once PM+infra confirm root cause and ETA for quota change.
anjali: Putting relevant logs and autoscaler traces into the incident doc (links: internal-runbook/PM-7882/logs).
ryan-oncall: Declaring incident mitigation stable. Queue depth back to baseline ~120. I'm leaving a post-incident action tracker in the ticket.
kate: Thanks all — :thumbsup: Great triage. Let's reconvene in the postmortem to lock in fixes.
incidents-bot: Incident marked: mitigated -> monitoring. Incident channel will remain open until postmortem complete.
ryan-oncall: End of live thread. Closing in channel but keeping ticket open for action items.
